tone_statements.citation: Wright, Jennifer. 2011. Tone in the Verb Phrase in Chrambo (Bambalang). Yaoundé: SIL Cameroon. 33 pp.
tone_statements.quote: Verb roots can be monosyllabic or disyllabic and can belong to one of two lexical tone classes: H tone and L tone verbs (see Wright 2009). All H tone verbs have an underlying H tone and L tone verbs have an underlying L tone, however the surface pitch of the verb roots vary greatly in context due to “grammatical tone” (i.e. the surface effects of underlying floating tone morphemes). All H tone verbs follow the same tone patterns as each other and all L tone verbs follow the same tone patterns as each other.
tone_statements.n_tones: 2 lexical verb classes (H, L); noun melodies H, L, HL, LH

tone_statements.citation: Luider, Jennifer. 2009. A Phonological Sketch of the Bambalang (Chrambo) Language. Yaoundé: SIL Cameroon. 43 pp.
tone_statements.quote: Chrambo has five phonetic pitches which can occur on syllables in isolation. These are high [á], low [à], falling [â], and rising [ǎ]. Mid tone is found in Chrambo, but as a result of downstep, rather than as an underlying tone. [...] Monosyllabic noun roots can have one of four patterns: H, L, LH, HL. Disyllabic noun roots can have one of six patterns: H H, L L, H L, L H, L LH, H HL. [...] Verbs can be grouped in one of two tone patterns, High and Low. Verbs in each group seem to pattern together for all the tenses.
tone_statements.locator: sec. 6 'Lexical Tone', p. 34; sec. 6.1.1 p. 35; sec. 6.2 p. 38
tone_statements.n_tones: 2 underlying levels (H, L) + contours HL, LH; 5 phonetic pitches incl. downstep…

tone.says: Grammatical tone in the VP: verb roots belong to two lexical tone classes (H, L; 64 minimal pairs among 612 single-root verbs); tense/aspect/mood markers are partly purely tonal (floating tones before/after the root) changing surface pitch on the verb and sometimes the subject; downstep distinguishes some negative tenses; summarises Luider 2009 noun melodies H, L, HL, LH (51 minimal noun pairs + 3 triplets by tone among 536 nouns); proposes lexical/grammatical tone marking for the orthography.
